modules.title: Query Optimization
modules.goal: Read plans, find the real bottleneck and improve queries with measurements.

topics.title: Optimization Process
topics.simple: Measure, read plan, change one thing, measure again.
topics.pro: Optimization starts with a slow query and its plan, not with guesses about indexes or configuration.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 10;

topics.title: EXPLAIN
topics.simple: EXPLAIN plan estimates dikhata hai.
topics.pro: EXPLAIN shows access paths, joins and costs without executing the query.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;

topics.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
topics.simple: EXPLAIN ANALYZE actual runtime dikhata hai.
topics.pro: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query and reports actual rows, loops and timing.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;

topics.title: Seq Scan
topics.simple: Seq scan poora table padhta hai.
topics.pro: A sequential scan reads every heap page and is often correct for small tables or large result fractions.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students;

topics.title: Index Scan
topics.simple: Index scan index se rows dhoondhta hai.
topics.pro: An index scan follows the index and fetches matching heap rows, ideal for selective predicates.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = 1;

topics.title: Bitmap Heap Scan
topics.simple: Bitmap scan medium selectivity ke liye hota hai.
topics.pro: A bitmap heap scan combines index matches and visits heap pages in physical order.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks BETWEEN 60 AND 70;

topics.title: Nested Loop
topics.simple: Nested loop small outer input ke liye achha hai.
topics.pro: A nested loop scans the inner side for each outer row, which is efficient when the outer set is small and the inner side is indexed.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id WHERE s.id = 1;

topics.title: Hash Join
topics.simple: Hash join large unsorted inputs ke liye hota hai.
topics.pro: A hash join builds a hash table from one input and probes it with the other, avoiding repeated inner scans.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id;

topics.title: Merge Join
topics.simple: Merge join sorted inputs ko merge karta hai.
topics.pro: A merge join reads both inputs in join-key order and merges them, often benefiting from indexes.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id ORDER BY s.id;

topics.title: Sort
topics.simple: Sort query ko order karta hai aur memory/disk use karta hai.
topics.pro: A Sort node appears when an index cannot provide the required order; large sorts spill to disk.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;

topics.title: HashAggregate
topics.simple: HashAggregate groups rows in memory.
topics.pro: A HashAggregate builds a hash table of groups, while GroupAggregate can use sorted input.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;

topics.title: Statistics
topics.simple: Planner statistics estimates banane ke liye use hote hain.
topics.pro: Row estimates, distinct counts and histograms drive join order and access-path choices.

example.sql: SELECT attname, n_distinct FROM pg_stats WHERE tablename = 'students';

topics.title: ANALYZE
topics.simple: ANALYZE statistics refresh karta hai.
topics.pro: ANALYZE samples table data and updates planner statistics without locking the table for long.

example.sql: ANALYZE students;

topics.title: Selectivity
topics.simple: Selectivity predicate ki filtering power hai.
topics.pro: High selectivity means few rows survive and usually favors an index; low selectivity favors a scan.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE email = 'a@example.com';

topics.title: CTE Materialization
topics.simple: CTE materialization plan ko badal sakta hai.
topics.pro: A materialized CTE is computed once and stored, which can help or hurt depending on reuse and row counts.

example.sql: EXPLAIN WITH avg_marks AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT AVG(marks) AS average FROM students) SELECT * FROM students, avg_marks WHERE marks > average;
example.output: A plan with a CTE Scan.

topics.title: Subquery Rewrites
topics.simple: Subquery ko join ya EXISTS me rewrite karo.
topics.pro: Correlated subqueries can become joins or semi-joins, often improving plans and avoiding repeated work.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT s.name FROM students s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e WHERE e.student_id = s.id);

topics.title: Join Order
topics.simple: Join order planner choose karta hai.
topics.pro: The planner reorders joins based on statistics and cost; written order is not execution order.
points: Do not force order by nesting.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id;

topics.title: Common Bottlenecks
topics.simple: Missing indexes, stale stats aur huge sorts common bottlenecks hain.
topics.pro: Most slow queries come from sequential scans on selective filters, bad estimates, missing join indexes or large sorts.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM enrollments ORDER BY enrolled_on DESC LIMIT 10;

topics.title: Benchmarking
topics.simple: Benchmark realistic data aur concurrency ke saath karo.
topics.pro: A benchmark needs realistic data volume, warm and cold cache runs, and concurrent load before it proves an improvement.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments;

topics.title: Practical Tuning
topics.simple: Slow query ko plan, index aur rewrite se tune karo.
topics.pro: A practical tuning loop documents the baseline, changes one thing, verifies the plan and measures the new runtime.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT s.name, COUNT(e.course_id) FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Optimization Process in a production query.
interview.answer: Optimization starts with a slow query and its plan, not with guesses about indexes or configuration. Key rules: Reproduce the query. Read the plan. Change one variable. Measure again.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain EXPLAIN in a production query.
interview.answer: EXPLAIN shows access paths, joins and costs without executing the query. Key rules: No execution. Estimates use statistics. Look for scans and sorts.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain EXPLAIN ANALYZE in a production query.
interview.answer: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query and reports actual rows, loops and timing. Key rules: It runs the query. Compare estimated and actual rows. Use BUFFERS for I/O detail.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Seq Scan in a production query.
interview.answer: A sequential scan reads every heap page and is often correct for small tables or large result fractions. Key rules: Good for large fractions. Bad for selective filters. Check table size.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Index Scan in a production query.
interview.answer: An index scan follows the index and fetches matching heap rows, ideal for selective predicates. Key rules: Good for few rows. Random I/O costs. Ordering may be free.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Bitmap Heap Scan in a production query.
interview.answer: A bitmap heap scan combines index matches and visits heap pages in physical order. Key rules: Good for medium selectivity. Combines indexes. Loses ordering.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Nested Loop in a production query.
interview.answer: A nested loop scans the inner side for each outer row, which is efficient when the outer set is small and the inner side is indexed. Key rules: Good for small outer sets. Index the inner join key. Watch loop counts.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Hash Join in a production query.
interview.answer: A hash join builds a hash table from one input and probes it with the other, avoiding repeated inner scans. Key rules: Good for large sets. Needs memory. No useful order.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Merge Join in a production query.
interview.answer: A merge join reads both inputs in join-key order and merges them, often benefiting from indexes. Key rules: Inputs must be sorted. Good for large ordered data. Can avoid a hash table.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Sort in a production query.
interview.answer: A Sort node appears when an index cannot provide the required order; large sorts spill to disk. Key rules: Watch sort method. Indexes can avoid sorts. LIMIT can reduce work.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain HashAggregate in a production query.
interview.answer: A HashAggregate builds a hash table of groups, while GroupAggregate can use sorted input. Key rules: Hash is common. Memory can spill. Sorted input favors GroupAggregate.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Statistics in a production query.
interview.answer: Row estimates, distinct counts and histograms drive join order and access-path choices. Key rules: Stale stats cause bad plans. ANALYZE refreshes them. Extended stats help correlations.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain ANALYZE in a production query.
interview.answer: ANALYZE samples table data and updates planner statistics without locking the table for long. Key rules: Run after large changes. It is cheap. Autovacuum does it automatically.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Selectivity in a production query.
interview.answer: High selectivity means few rows survive and usually favors an index; low selectivity favors a scan. Key rules: Unique predicates are selective. Planner estimates matter. Use real data.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain CTE Materialization in a production query.
interview.answer: A materialized CTE is computed once and stored, which can help or hurt depending on reuse and row counts. Key rules: MATERIALIZED forces it. NOT MATERIALIZED inlines it. Measure both.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Subquery Rewrites in a production query.
interview.answer: Correlated subqueries can become joins or semi-joins, often improving plans and avoiding repeated work. Key rules: EXISTS is a semi-join. JOIN can duplicate rows. Measure the rewrite.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Join Order in a production query.
interview.answer: The planner reorders joins based on statistics and cost; written order is not execution order. Key rules: Do not force order by nesting. Keep statistics fresh. Read the actual plan.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Common Bottlenecks in a production query.
interview.answer: Most slow queries come from sequential scans on selective filters, bad estimates, missing join indexes or large sorts. Key rules: Check scans. Check estimates. Check sorts.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Benchmarking in a production query.
interview.answer: A benchmark needs realistic data volume, warm and cold cache runs, and concurrent load before it proves an improvement. Key rules: Use real data size. Measure multiple runs. Watch concurrency.

interview.q: Module 27 · Explain Practical Tuning in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical tuning loop documents the baseline, changes one thing, verifies the plan and measures the new runtime. Key rules: Baseline first. Change one thing. Verify the plan. Record the result.

debug.title: Stale statistics
debug.broken: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
debug.fix:
ANALYZE students;
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
debug.error: The estimate may be far from reality

debug.title: Missing join index
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id WHERE s.id = 1;

debug.title: Sort without index
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC LIMIT 10;
debug.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_students_marks ON students (marks DESC);
debug.error: The query sorts the whole table

debug.title: Function on column
debug.error: The plain email index is not used

debug.title: OR prevents index
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks = 90 OR name = 'Aarav';
debug.error: The OR may force a sequential scan

debug.title: Wide SELECT
debug.fix: SELECT id, name FROM students WHERE marks > 90;

debug.title: LIMIT without ORDER BY
debug.fix: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY id LIMIT 10;

debug.title: Nested loop explosion
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id;
debug.fix: Ensure both join keys are indexed and compare the plan at realistic volume.
debug.error: The inner side is scanned for every outer row

debug.title: CTE materialized unnecessarily
debug.broken: WITH big AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM enrollments) SELECT * FROM big WHERE course_id = 10;
debug.fix: WITH big AS NOT MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM enrollments) SELECT * FROM big WHERE course_id = 10;
debug.error: The CTE is fully materialized before filtering

debug.title: EXPLAIN without execution
debug.broken: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
debug.fix: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
